interpretation: The existing native alpha0.25 anchor retains75% of the generated residual. Reproduction establishes that the current cache and baseline pipeline are aligned; SR Q4 anchoring is a different operator.

GT pooled-MSE oracle t varies strongly: compression0.0630, deblur0.1057, denoise0.2733, SR0.2907, identity0, near-clean0.00329-0.00383. These are post-hoc diagnostic coefficients, not predictions or a deployable selection rule.

Fixed t0.05 improves mean-frame PSNR on all four ordinary examples, but worsens the repeated identity by about2.191dB and near-clean by about0.48-0.50dB relative to R_phi-only. All positive fixed-grid coefficients harm these controls relative to R_phi-only in pooled MSE and MAE. This does not mean all small mixtures are worse than the near-clean INPUT; keep both baselines visible.

Ordinary deblur at t0.05 gains PSNR while its MAE worsens. A pooled-MSE oracle also does not optimize mean-frame PSNR. Distortion metrics can disagree even before LPIPS or temporal quality is examined.

The result supports magnitude-sensitive action evaluation as a useful control diagnostic, but not an independent novelty claim, a calibrated harm certificate, a universally safe t, or omni generalization.
